title: metadata-protocol: rollbackMetaItem / revertCommit restore a version without the save-door refusal family, so a restore can re-create a refused shape
body:
Filing gate **③**: an observation of the contract review of PR #25257 (record 6347940824, observation 1), disposed in the seat's ACCEPT 6348040277 (item 5). Pre-existing door shape; it does not block that PR, which merged as `bda53bb0b` (card #25211).
- **Who acts:** `domain:engine`.
- **Dedupe:** none found.

## What happens on `main` (at `bda53bb0b`)
- `saveMetaItem` runs a family of save-door refusals after the Zod gate: the `external` binding on a managed datasource (#25168, #25257), the default record page, hook bodies, elevated flows, and others.
- The restore doors (`rollbackMetaItem`, `revertCommit`; see the door list at `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:137`) write a history body back through `repo.restoreVersion` (`:7254` onward) and do not ask that family. A restore of a version saved before a refusal existed — or of the other half of a pair (an object version that binds `external` while its datasource is now managed) — re-creates the refused shape.

## Wanted
- Measure first: which refusals the restore doors already re-judge (some restore paths call a judge on the history body, `:7265`–`:7284`) and which they skip; list them.
- The restore doors refuse what `saveMetaItem` refuses, through the same judges (one copy each), with the same envelope; or a written reason per refusal why a restore may bypass it.

## Acceptance
- Pinned: restoring a version that the save door would refuse answers the save door's refusal and stores nothing; restoring an acceptable version still succeeds.
- No refusal is copied: the restore path calls the same function the save door calls.
